relevance_reason: The title says the paper reports a new SENP7 missense variant in a case of fatal arthrogryposis multiplex congenita with immunodeficiency, which is this entry's disorder. However, the supplied abstract is cut off, so only very little can be extracted.

findings.statement: Pal et al. (2025) reported a novel missense variant in the SENP7 gene in a patient with fatal arthrogryposis multiplex congenita and immunodeficiency. They also compared the main clinical features and molecular findings of their case with those of previously reported cases of SENP7-associated disorder.
quotes: SENP7-Related Fatal Arthrogryposis Multiplex Congenita and Immunodeficiency: A Novel Missense Variation and Syndromic Delineation.
of prominent clinical features and molecular findings of SENP7-associated disorder in previous cases and our case.

relevance_reason: Reports a family with a lethal prenatal arthrogryposis phenotype caused by a homozygous SENP7 stop-gain variant, which widens the AMC9 spectrum.

findings.statement: Saad et al. (2025) described a consanguineous Egyptian family with a history of 3 fetal deaths, all with multiple congenital anomalies. Ultrasound of the current fetus showed similar anomalies, including arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, CNS malformations, congenital heart disease, and renal anomalies. The authors described this as the first full prenatal description of a lethal syndrome linked to SENP7.
quotes: a consanguineous Egyptian family with a history of three fetal deaths, all presenting with multiple congenital anomalies
Similar anomalies were observed through ultrasound assessment of the current fetus, including arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, CNS malformations, congenital heart disease, and renal anomalies.

findings.statement: In fetal DNA from a consanguineous Egyptian family with recurrent lethal multiple congenital anomalies including arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, Saad et al. (2025) used singleton exome sequencing to identify a homozygous stop-gain variant in the SENP7 gene (c.745C>T, p.Arg249Ter). The resulting premature termination codon was predicted to cause nonsense-mediated decay of the mutant mRNA. The authors proposed that this impairs SENP7's isopeptidase activity in deconjugating polySUMO chains.
quotes: a novel homozygous stop-gain variant in SENP7 c.745C>T; p.(Arg249*)

Singleton exome sequencing (ES) of fetal DNA revealed a SENP7 variant allele, which results in a premature termination codon, and the mutant mRNA is predicted to be degraded by nonsense-mediated decay (NMD).
This leads to impaired gene function, particularly disrupting SENP7's isopeptidase activity in deconjugating polySUMO chains.

relevance_reason: Reports a consanguineous family with lethal AMC caused by a homozygous (recessive) splice site variant in SENP7, the gene for AMC9.

findings.statement: Kotecha et al. (2025) reported a consanguineous family with multiple members affected by a severe, lethal form of arthrogryposis multiplex congenita.
quotes: We report a consanguineous family with multiple affected members with AMC
expanding the spectrum of SENP7 as a causative gene in rare cases of lethal AMC

findings.statement: In affected members of a consanguineous family with lethal arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, Kotecha et al. (2025) identified a recessive variant in the highly conserved splice donor site of SENP7 that resulted in mis-splicing of the affected exons. The authors stated that this was a noncoding splice site variant in SENP7.
quotes: identified a recessive mutation in the highly conserved splice donor site, resulting in the mis-splicing of the affected exons
This is a reported case of an affected family with a noncoding, splice site SENP7 variant

findings.statement: Kotecha et al. (2025) noted that SENP7 is a deSUMOylase that is critical for sarcomere assembly and skeletal muscle contraction by regulating the transcriptional program in skeletal muscle.
quotes: SENP7 is a deSUMOylase that is critical for sarcomere assembly and skeletal muscle contraction by regulating the transcriptional program in the skeletal muscle.

relevance_reason: Reports homozygous loss-of-function SENP7 variants in 4 children from 3 families with immunodeficiency, neurodevelopmental abnormalities and dysmorphism, which defines this entry.

findings.statement: Kobayashi et al. (2024) reported 4 children from 3 unrelated families who had neurodevelopmental abnormalities, dysmorphism, and immunodeficiency. Their clinical presentations were characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia and intermittent neutropenia, and all 4 patients died in infancy.
quotes: 4 children from 3 unrelated families presenting with neurodevelopmental abnormalities, dysmorphism, and immunodeficiency
Their clinical presentations were characterized by hypogammaglobulinemia, intermittent neutropenia, and ultimately death in infancy for all 4 patients.

findings.statement: Kobayashi et al. (2024), through international collaboration to evaluate a novel candidate disease gene, identified rare homozygous loss-of-function variants in the SENP7 gene in 4 children from 3 unrelated families with immunodeficiency and neurologic and muscular phenotypes.
quotes: identified rare, biallelic, specifically homozygous, loss of function variants in SENP7 in 4 children from 3 unrelated families

findings.statement: Kobayashi et al. (2024) noted that SENP7 is a sentrin-specific protease involved in deSUMOylation, a posttranslational modification of proteins essential for cell regulation, and proposed that deficiency of deSUMOylation may represent a novel mechanism of primary immunodeficiency.
quotes: SENP7 is a sentrin-specific protease involved in posttranslational modification of proteins essential for cell regulation, via a process referred to as deSUMOylation.
We propose that deficiency of deSUMOylation may represent a novel mechanism of primary immunodeficiency.

relevance_reason: This paper reports the family that defines AMC9: four affected infants with a homozygous SENP7 stop-gain variant, plus functional studies in patient fibroblasts.

findings.statement: Samra et al. (2023) described a kindred with 4 affected infants who had congenital arthrogryposis, did not reach any developmental milestones, and had early respiratory failure, neutropenia, and recurrent infections. All 4 died within 4 months after birth.
quotes: We identified a kindred with four affected subjects presenting with a spectrum of findings including congenital arthrogryposis, no achievement of developmental milestones, early respiratory failure, neutropenia and recurrent infections. All died within four months after birth.

phenotypes.text: death within four months after birth

findings.statement: In the 4 affected members of a kindred with fatal arthrogryposis multiplex congenita, early respiratory failure, and neutropenia, Samra et al. (2023) used exome sequencing and segregation studies to identify a homozygous stop-gain variant in the SENP7 gene (c.1474C>T, p.Gln492Ter), which they considered the probable cause. Fibroblasts from the proband showed reduced SENP7 mRNA expression.
quotes: Exome sequencing identified a homozygous stop gain variant in SENP7 c.1474C>T; p.(Gln492*) as the probable aetiology.
We performed exome sequencing and segregation studies in a family with several infants presenting with an unidentified syndrome.
The proband's fibroblasts demonstrated decreased mRNA expression.

findings.statement: Samra et al. (2023) found significant protein dysregulation in total cell lysates and in the chromatin fraction of fibroblasts from a patient homozygous for a SENP7 stop-gain variant. HP1-alpha, several histones, and H3K9me3 were reduced. The authors suggested that loss of SENP7 reduces heterochromatin condensation and leads to aberrant gene expression, and that SENP7 has a critical role in nervous system development, hematopoiesis, and immune function.
quotes: Protein expression studies showed significant protein dysregulation in total cell lysates and in the chromatin fraction. We found that HP1α levels as well as different histones and H3K9me3 were reduced in patient fibroblasts.
suggest loss of SENP7 leads to reduced heterochromatin condensation and subsequent aberrant gene expression.
Our results suggest a critical role for SENP7 in nervous system development, haematopoiesis and immune function in humans.
